newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain protests Chinese plans to scrap HK laws.
newsitem.headline: Britain protests Chinese plans to scrap HK laws.

text.p: The British envoy responsible for Hong Kong's transition to Chinese rule said he would express concerns about a proposal to water down the colony's civil liberties when he meets his Chinese counterpart on Friday.
Hugh Davies, leader of the British delegation on the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group (JLG) responsible for transitional matters, called on Chinese team leader Zhao Jihua on Friday morning.

"As you know, I am coming to talk to ambassador Zhao about our concern about the proposal by the legal sub-group of (China's) Preparatory Committee to repeal and to amend a number of laws," Davies told reporters.
The laws facing the axe when Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 include parts of the Bill of Rights and legislation allowing freedom of assembly and association.
Zhao accused the British of "staging a show".
"I feel very unhappy today. The British told the press about our meeting without asking me," Zhao told reporters minutes after Davies arrived at the Chinese JLG office.
"Their purpose is to stage a show."
The meeting continued on Friday afternoon.
Pro-democracy activists held a protest against China's plans on Friday. Hong Kong has been a British colony for more than 150 years.
